candidates.title: The infra-genericity gate matches one engine's vocabulary rather than the engine-concept rule it enforces, so a sibling engine's nouns and an underscore-joined identifier both pass unflagged

evidence.command: git show 077dbe2c:scripts/ci/check-infra-genericity.sh | sed -n '9,11p;79p'; git grep -n 'cut_nz_per_col' 077dbe2c -- crates/cobre-solver/src/freeze.rs
evidence.output:
#

# identifiers like "execution", "cuts_active", "cutting_edge"):
-- :79 --
PATTERN='\bSddp\b|\bsddp\b|\bSDDP\b|\bBenders\b|\bCut\b|\bcut\b|cut pool|cutting-plane|cutting[.]plane|outer approximation|CutSync[[:alnum:]_]*|CutSelection[[:alnum:]_]*|\bMetadataCuts\b'
-- freeze.rs --
crates/cobre-solver/src/freeze.rs:22:    pub cut_nz_per_col: Vec<u32>,
crates/cobre-solver/src/freeze.rs:137, :138, :141, :188 (production uses)
evidence.reading: The script states its own reason for the word boundaries at :10-11: they are deliberate, chosen to avoid false positives on identifiers like `execution`, `cuts_active` and `cutting_edge`, where the letters `cut` are incidental. That rationale is sound for those three, and the design is not naive. The gap is a different one. `\bcut\b` requires a non-word character after `cut`; `_` is a word character, so `cut_nz_per_col` never matches, and the gate exits 0 at the pin (solver+comm station handoff: exit 0, "OK: no algorithm-specific vocabulary found in infrastructure crates."). But `cut_nz_per_col` is NOT an incidental-letters false positive of the `execution` kind: it is declared as `FreezeScratch.cut_nz_per_col: Vec<u32>` at freeze.rs:22 and used in production at :137, :138, :141 and :188 as a per-column count of cut-row non-zeros in the frozen LP. The word `cut` there denotes exactly the Benders cut row the rule forbids naming in cobre-solver -- it is the engine concept, spelled in snake_case. Separately, PATTERN enumerates the nouns of ONE engine (Sddp, Benders, Cut, cut pool, cutting-plane, outer approximation, CutSync*, CutSelection*, MetadataCuts). CLAUDE.md:41 states the rule as "zero algorithm-specific references", which is a concept test; the gate implements a fixed vocabulary of one algorithm, so a future sibling engine's vocabulary in an L0/L1 crate passes silently.

candidates.fixShape: Sharpen the existing gate in place; the vocabulary half of the leak belongs to the solver+comm station, the gate half is here. Two independent moves. First, close the snake_case hole without losing the deliberate false-positive protection the script's own :10-11 rationale buys: the boundary needs to treat an underscore as a word separator for the engine nouns rather than as a word character, so `cut_nz_per_col` matches while `cuts_active` and `cutting_edge` still do not. Second, make the vocabulary's single-engine scope explicit rather than implicit: the rule prose says "algorithm-specific", so the gate should carry a named, reviewable list of engine vocabularies with an obvious place for a second engine's nouns, so that adding an engine forces a visible edit instead of inheriting silent coverage. Both stay inside the one blocking gate and its one `quality-scripts` step; neither needs a new gate, a new scan library, or a rename in cobre-solver (the rename decision is the register entry's, not this station's).

the declaration `FreezeScratch.cut_nz_per_col: Vec<u32>` -- the live evader, pre-seeded by the solver+comm station; cited, never anchored (rule 8)

candidates.title: No CI workflow runs on a pull request into develop, so every blocking gate first sees a develop change only after it has already merged

evidence.command: git show 077dbe2c:.github/workflows/ci.yml | sed -n '3,7p'; git grep -n 'pull_request' 077dbe2c -- .github/workflows; git show 077dbe2c:scripts/ci/check-allow-rationale.sh | sed -n '368p;422p'
evidence.output:
on:
  push:
    branches: [main, develop]
  pull_request:
    branches: [main]
-- check-allow-rationale.sh --
BASE_REF="${BASE_REF:-origin/main}"
    done < <(git -C "$REPO_ROOT" diff --unified=0 "${BASE}"...HEAD -- 'crates/*/src/*.rs')
evidence.reading: The trigger block is asymmetric: `push` covers main AND develop (:4-5), `pull_request` covers main only (:6-7). A pull request whose base is develop therefore triggers no ci.yml run; the first evaluation of that change happens on the post-merge push. All 14 jobs are affected, including the 13 blocking gates wired in `quality-scripts` (:248-300) -- genericity (:262), cut-selection determinism (:264), comment refs (:276), doc paths (:274), plan leaks (:270), python parity (:294), doc voice (:296) -- plus clippy (:154), fmt (:246), schemas (:339) and docs-examples (:360). A failure on develop is detected on a branch that already contains the defect, so the gate reports rather than prevents. The E4 allow-rationale gate compounds this: its base is `git merge-base HEAD origin/main` (:368) over `crates/*/src/*.rs` (:422), so on a develop push its diff window is the whole develop-versus-main delta rather than the one change, and its per-change scoping is lost exactly where the PR run is missing.

candidates.fixShape: One sentence, as the probe directs: the trigger list is the owner's call, and the shape that removes the asymmetry is to have the pull_request trigger cover the same branch set the push trigger already covers. Everything else follows from that one edit; no job, gate or script changes.

-- cobre-sddp/Cargo.toml --
slow-tests = []
test-support = ["cobre-core/test-support"]
cobre-core = { version = "0.15.0", path = "../cobre-core", features = ["test-support"] }
-- cobre-sddp/src/lib.rs :46-47 --
#[cfg(any(test, feature = "test-support"))]
pub mod test_support;
-- tests/parity.rs --
752: mod determinism {
894:             cobre_sddp::test_support::fill_consistent_basis(out);
-- ci.yml :114 --
      - run: cargo test --workspace --features "${{ env.NON_SOLVER_FEATURES }}"
evidence.reading: Four facts compose into a dead path. (1) Both workflow invocations pass features but not `test-support`: `--features slow-tests` at :34 and `--no-default-features --features "clp slow-tests"` at :55. (2) `pub mod test_support` in the library is gated `#[cfg(any(test, feature = "test-support"))]` at lib.rs:46-47; an integration test links the library built WITHOUT cfg(test), so the module exists only when the feature is passed. (3) The `parity` target needs it unconditionally: `mod determinism` at parity.rs:752 is ungated (line 751 is blank, 750 closes the preceding module) and calls `cobre_sddp::test_support::fill_consistent_basis` at :894, with three further unconditional uses at :1303, :1437 and :1461. (4) The crate's own `test-support` feature at Cargo.toml:55 is not reachable by accident: the dev-dependency at :77 enables `cobre-core/test-support`, a DIFFERENT crate's feature, which does not turn on cobre-sddp's. So both dispatched commands fail at compile time, before any shuffle test is selected. The automatic suite does not compensate: the five shuffle tests carry a plain `#[ignore = "full shuffle matrix -- dispatched via invariance-shuffle.yml"]` (parity.rs:139, :145, :151, :157, :163 -- not the slow-tests cfg_attr form used elsewhere), and ci.yml:114 runs `cargo test --workspace` with no `--include-ignored`, so they are skipped there too. The workflow is also `workflow_dispatch`-only, with the nightly schedule commented out at :5-7, so nothing ever surfaces the compile failure automatically. Net: the declaration-order-invariance contract at CLAUDE.md:26-31 has a shuffle matrix that no CI path can execute.

candidates.fixShape: Amend the two existing run lines so the feature set they pass actually satisfies the target they name: the parity binary needs the crate's own `test-support` feature alongside the backend and slow-tests features, on both the primary-backend and the secondary-backend invocation. That is the whole compile fix. Two further decisions surround it and are named, not taken here. First, the ignore form: these five tests use a bare ignore rather than the slow-tests cfg_attr pattern the rest of the crate uses, which is why the automatic suite cannot reach them even with the workspace feature set; converting them to the crate's established gating form would let the main suite run them whenever the feature is on, and would make the dispatch-only workflow a convenience rather than the sole path. Second, the trigger: a manually dispatched workflow cannot report a regression nobody dispatched, so the owner should decide between restoring the commented-out schedule and folding the matrix into an automatically triggered job. A cheap guard against the whole class is worth stating: an automatically triggered compile-only step over this test target would have caught the missing feature immediately, since the failure is at compile time and needs no shuffle run.

`mod determinism {` is ungated, so its test-support uses are unconditional for the whole parity target
the first unconditional `cobre_sddp::test_support::fill_consistent_basis` call; :1303, :1437 and :1461 are the others
the bare `#[ignore = "full shuffle matrix -- dispatched via invariance-shuffle.yml"]`, repeated at :145 :151 :157 :163 -- the reason ci.yml:114 skips these tests

candidates.title: The CLI template mirror is guarded in one direction only: a file added to the canonical example deck but not to the embedded list leaves both guards green while cobre init ships an incomplete case

evidence.command: git show 077dbe2c:crates/cobre-cli/build.rs | sed -n '8,9p;16p'; git show 077dbe2c:scripts/ci/check-docs-examples.sh | sed -n '32p;111,116p'; git grep -nE 'diff -r|diff -ru|cmp ' 077dbe2c -- scripts .github/workflows; git grep -n 'examples/1dtoy' 077dbe2c -- scripts .github/workflows
evidence.output:
-- build.rs --
//! The canonical source for these files is `examples/1dtoy/` at the workspace
//! root. The copies in `templates/1dtoy/` must be kept in sync.
const TEMPLATE_FILES: &[&str] = &[
-- check-docs-examples.sh --
readonly EXPECTED_INPUT_FILES=11
# Invariant 1: init materializes exactly the expected file count
"$BIN" init --template "$TEMPLATE" "$CASE_DIR" >/dev/null
actual_files="$(find "$CASE_DIR" -type f | wc -l | tr -d '[:space:]')"
if [[ "$actual_files" -ne "$EXPECTED_INPUT_FILES" ]]; then
  fail "`cobre init --template $TEMPLATE` wrote $actual_files input files, expected $EXPECTED_INPUT_FILES. ..."
-- diff -r / cmp across scripts and workflows --
scripts/ci/check_schemas.sh:31 (the only recursive diff in the corpus; it compares schemas/, not the template trees)
-- examples/1dtoy references in scripts and workflows --
(no hit: no script or workflow reads examples/1dtoy)
evidence.reading: build.rs:8-9 states the invariant in prose -- `examples/1dtoy/` is canonical and `templates/1dtoy/` must be kept in sync BY HAND -- and `const TEMPLATE_FILES` is the embedded enumeration. Content equality IS guarded, and the naive claim that nothing checks it is false: a unit test byte-compares each embedded file against the canonical file on disk and runs in the workspace suite (see positives). The surviving hole is directional. Both guards iterate the embedded set: the unit test walks the embedded files and asserts each matches its canonical counterpart, and the shell gate at :113 counts the files that `cobre init` WROTE and compares that count to `EXPECTED_INPUT_FILES=11` -- which is the embedded cardinality, so the assert is a tautology with respect to TEMPLATE_FILES and says nothing about the canonical tree. Nothing reads the canonical directory: no script or workflow mentions `examples/1dtoy` at all, and the corpus's only recursive diff is check_schemas.sh:31 over `schemas/`. Consequence: add a twelfth file to `examples/1dtoy/` and forget TEMPLATE_FILES, and every guard stays green while `cobre init --template 1dtoy` silently produces a deck the documented canonical case does not match.

candidates.fixShape: Amend the existing blocking gate rather than adding one. The gate already has the canonical directory available at the workspace root and already knows the template name, so the missing assertion is a set comparison rather than a count: compare the file set the canonical directory contains against the file set `cobre init` materializes, and fail when either side has a member the other lacks. That subsumes the current count assert, removes the hand-maintained expected-count literal from the script, and closes the direction the unit test cannot see because the unit test's iteration domain is the embedded list itself. The build script's prose invariant at :8-9 then describes something a gate enforces instead of something a person remembers.

citedContext.why: `fn test_1dtoy_embedded_files_match_canonical_source()` -- the content-equality guard that does exist; it iterates only the embedded template files, which is why the canonical-to-embedded direction is unguarded. Cited, never anchored (rule 8)
the `assert_eq!(file.content, on_disk.as_slice(), ...)` byte comparison, reached via `std::fs::read` at :210 against `concat!(env!("CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR"), "/../../examples/1dtoy")` at :206

evidence.reading: Every clippy invocation in the repository is `--workspace` (ci.yml:154 in the `clippy` job at :116, ci.yml:221 in the `clp` job at :166); `git grep` finds no third one and none with `--manifest-path`. Those are clippy tool lints: rustc ignores them, so the one CI compile of this crate, `cargo test --manifest-path crates/cobre-python/Cargo.toml` at :567, does not evaluate them either. CLAUDE.md:20-21 lists both as non-negotiable hard rules (":17 -- These are non-negotiable"). The crate is not in breach at the pin: all ten `.unwrap()` occurrences in its sources sit in a test module covered by an explicit allow, so this is an uncovered surface rather than a live violation -- the clippy job would stay green if that changed. The asymmetry is sharpest against the E4 gate, which is blocking at ci.yml:292 and scopes its diff to `crates/*/src/*.rs` at check-allow-rationale.sh:422: that glob DOES match the bindings crate, so a new `#[allow(clippy::...)]` there must carry a written rationale for a lint no CI job ever runs, and the crate already carries around twenty such suppressions. candidates.fixShape: Amend the job that already exists rather than reopening the exclusion. The workspace exclusion is sanctioned and states its own reason, so the fix is not to make the crate a member; it is to give the crate the same lint pass every member gets, at the one place in CI that already builds it with a Python interpreter present. The python job already compiles this crate against its own manifest for the Rust tests, on a single matrix entry, so a clippy pass over the same manifest with warnings denied belongs beside that step and inherits its interpreter and its backend feature selection. Two secondary points for the owner. The same membership boundary means the crate is outside the documentation-warning bar as well, so whoever adds the clippy pass should decide whether a docs pass over the manifest is worth the minutes, given that the crate's rustdoc is user-facing for Python readers. And once clippy runs, the roughly twenty existing clippy suppressions in the crate become meaningful for the first time, so expect the first run to surface work; that is the finding, not a side effect of the fix.
